messages:
Ashley: seeing a weird fd/conn spike on apiserver in eu-central1 right after we started a bulk GPU reclaim job, apiserver p99 latency -> 1.2s and some 503s. any ideas?
Mike: ugh, saw that too. controller-manager started constantly trying leader election -> backoff. logs show lots of 'accept: too many open files' on apiserver. :face_with_raised_eyebrow:
Dinesh: confirmed. etctd write latency also spiked ~30s at the same time (fsync backlog). sounds like capacity storm + kernel fd exhaustion.
sre-bot: alert: apiserver.fds_in_use > 48000 (threshold 45000) in eu-central1 at 2025-03-12T09:07:30Z
Maya: timeline: 09:05 we kicked reclaim-job-gpu-bulk, 09:06 node-terminations start, 09:07 apiserver fd spike and 503s, 09:09 controller-manager leader flips.
Ashley: pasted a short excerpt from apiserver stderr: 
```
accept: accept4: too many open files
2025-03-12 09:07:31 server.go:120] handled connection error: accept tcp [::]:6443: accept4: too many open files
```
Dinesh: and etcd logs show repeated WAL fsync stalls: 
```
2025-03-12T09:07:28Z etcdserver: apply entries took too long: 31.2s
2025-03-12T09:07:29Z wal: fsync took 32s
```
Mike: hypothesis: bulk GPU reclaim caused many pods to terminate/reconnect, kubelet transient connections -> apiserver conn churn -> fd exhaustion + underlying NVMe burst causing WAL/fsync jitter on etcd nodes (co-located storage heavy hosts).
Maya: quick mitigation applied: scaled apiserver replicas from 3 -> 6 in eu-central1, bumped systemd LimitNOFILE for kube-apiserver, temporarily rate-limited reclaim job to 10 nodes/min, and added fencing on heavy-provision cron.
Ashley: after scale and rate-limit, error rates fell: apiserver p99 back to 120ms, fd count dropped to ~14k. controller-manager stabilized.
Dinesh: follow-ups: 1) add pre-check on bulk reclaim jobs to query control-plane fd/headroom and etcd io saturation, 2) tune etcd WAL fsync IO QoS on storage class for control plane, 3) add alert for leader-election-flip-rate and apiserver fd pressure.
Mike: also recommend moving GPU reclaim off-peak and adding jittered termination to avoid synchronized kubelet reconnect storms.
Maya: I'll file infra ticket to: increase apiserver NOFILE via systemd unit in the image, add reclaim job governor, and create an incident runbook entry for "apiserver fd storm during batch node operations".
Ashley: linking to the small dashboard we used: https://grafana.internal/r/controlplane?orgId=1&var-region=eu-central1 (shows fd, p99, etcd fsync). :thumbsup:
Dinesh: one more thing — check conntrack table size on iptables nodes, we saw conntrack churn; bumping nf_conntrack hashsize gave extra headroom.
Maya: assigning tasks: DINESH -> IO/QoS ticket, MIKE -> reclaim job throttle, ASHLEY -> runbook + dashboard update. will sync tomorrow at 09:00 UTC.
sre-bot: incident created: INC-20250312-1423 (severity: medium)
